links.outcome: Hallucination rate and accuracy of LLM with evidence retrieval grounding versus standalone LLM and standard RAG
links.effect: MEGA-RAG reduced hallucination rates by over 40% versus baselines; highest accuracy 0.7913, precision 0.7541, recall 0.8304, F1 0.7904.
links.quote: Experimental evaluation demonstrates that MEGA-RAG outperforms four baseline models [PubMedBERT, PubMedGPT, standalone LLM, and LLM with standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)], achieving a reduction in hallucination rates by over 40%.

unlisted_practices: multi-source evidence retrieval (dense, keyword, knowledge graph) with cross-encoder reranking
discrepancy-aware answer refinement module to correct hallucinations

screen.reason: Empirically benchmarks a multi-evidence retrieval-augmented generation and discrepancy refinement framework against baseline LLMs to reduce hallucination in public health tasks.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation grounding and answer refinement
